text.p: French pay television company Canal Plus, which announced an 11 percent increase in 1996 profits on Wednesday, said the cost of absorbing Dutch-based Nethold would leave it close to breakeven in 1997.

Canal Plus 1996 net attributable profit climbed to 741 million francs from 666 million francs in 1995, broadly in line with expectations, and the company said it was maintaining its net dividend at 20 francs per share.
However, analysts had said while they expected a healthy increase in 1996 profits, the impact of the Nethold merger on 1997 profits would be the most important factor.
"This expansion should weigh significantly on Canal Plus's results, as Nethold's activities are in a growth phase that requires substantial investments," Canal Plus said in a statement.

Laurent Perpere, Canal Plus finance director, told Reuters, "Since the announcement of the merger with Nethold, we have always said we would have a net attributable profit, excluding exceptional items, close to breakeven."
Canal Plus will hold a shareholders meeting on Thursday to approve the merger an the nomination of three Nethold officials to the French company's board.

Canal Plus also said the group's balance sheet was significantly modified in 1996 due to substantial investments, notably for the formation of a base of digital terminals and the acquisitions of UGC and the Carolco film library.
It said net fixed assets rose by 3.6 billion francs and revenues climbed 14.5 percent to 11.6 billion francs.
